metadata.title: COMP1010 Python theory practice
metadata.coverage_note: Full extracted lecture text inventoried. Image-only content has not been visually verified; see coverage.csv. Question count includes related practice variants, not that many independent concepts.
metadata.grading: One correct option per question. Assertions enabled. Each snippet is a fresh program. repr is explicit where used; preserve quotes and whitespace.

questions.prompt: Which component executes Python code?
questions.explanation: An interpreter executes Python instructions; an editor helps create source files.

questions.prompt: What is the usual filename extension of a Python source script?
questions.explanation: A Python source module or script normally uses .py.

questions.prompt: What does IDLE stand for?
questions.explanation: IDLE provides an editor, shell and debugger.

questions.prompt: Which environment is designed around executable notebook cells?
questions.explanation: Jupyter notebooks combine executable cells with explanatory material.

questions.prompt: Which tool provides an enhanced interactive Python shell?
questions.explanation: IPython provides interactive execution features.

questions.prompt: Which feature is associated with an IDE such as PyCharm?

options.text: Automatic proof of all program correctness
Conversion of all Python code into HTML

questions.explanation: An IDE integrates development tools but cannot guarantee correctness.

questions.prompt: What makes VS Code extensible?

options.text: A built-in proof that code is correct
A requirement that every file be Python

questions.explanation: Extensions add language and development capabilities.

questions.prompt: Which task is Matplotlib primarily associated with?
questions.explanation: Matplotlib is a plotting library.

questions.prompt: Which library is primarily associated with numerical arrays?
questions.explanation: NumPy supplies numerical array operations and is an external package.

questions.prompt: Which library is primarily associated with tabular data analysis?
questions.explanation: pandas provides data-analysis structures and operations.

questions.prompt: Which symbol begins a Python comment outside a string literal?
questions.explanation: A # starts a comment up to the end of the physical line when outside a string.

questions.prompt: What is a literal?

options.text: A value written directly in source code

questions.explanation: Examples include 7, 2.5 and 'hello'.

questions.prompt: Which statement about expressions is correct?

options.text: Every expression must print a value
Python evaluates an expression to a value

questions.explanation: Evaluation and printing are different actions.

questions.prompt: Which operator performs exponentiation?
questions.explanation: In Python ** raises to a power; ^ is bitwise XOR.

questions.prompt: Which operator performs floor division?
questions.explanation: Floor division rounds the quotient toward negative infinity.

questions.prompt: Which operator checks object identity?
questions.explanation: is tests whether two references designate the same object.

questions.prompt: Which operator checks membership?
questions.explanation: Membership tests depend on the container; for strings this tests substrings.

questions.prompt: Which logical operator always produces a bool?
questions.explanation: and and or can return operands; not returns True or False.

questions.prompt: Why can 0.1 + 0.2 differ from 0.3?

options.text: Python treats + as concatenation for floats
Many decimal fractions are approximated in binary floating point
All floats are stored as decimal strings

questions.explanation: Binary floating-point representation can introduce rounding error.

questions.prompt: Which is the correct interpretation of 'ab' * 3?

options.text: A deep copy of a list

questions.explanation: Repetition produces 'ababab'; it is not generally described as shallow copying.

questions.prompt: What does type(value) return?
questions.explanation: For example type(3) is the int type object.

questions.prompt: What does assignment bind in Python?

options.text: A fixed type permanently to a name
A new independent copy in every case
A print command to a file

questions.explanation: Assignment binds a name and does not generally copy the object.

questions.prompt: Must a variable be declared with a type before first assignment?
questions.explanation: Ordinary Python assignment introduces a binding without a prior type declaration.

questions.prompt: Which is a valid variable name?
questions.explanation: Letters, underscores and noninitial digits are valid; keywords cannot be identifiers.

questions.prompt: Which names refer to distinct bindings?

options.text: Any names with the same length

questions.explanation: Python identifiers are case-sensitive.

questions.prompt: What does int() do to a finite float's fractional part?

options.text: Always rounds to the nearest integer

questions.explanation: For example int(-3.8) is -3.

questions.prompt: Which is an example of explicit type conversion?
questions.explanation: An explicit conversion calls a conversion function.

questions.prompt: What is the type returned by input() after successful input?

options.text: It depends on whether the input looks numeric

questions.explanation: Numeric input must be explicitly converted when numeric operations are required.

questions.prompt: What does rebinding radius do to an already computed numeric area variable?

options.text: It does not automatically recompute area
It turns area into a function

questions.explanation: Assignment stores the evaluated result, not a spreadsheet-style formula.

questions.prompt: Which prefix denotes a hexadecimal integer literal?
questions.explanation: 0x and 0X denote hexadecimal literals.

questions.prompt: Which prefix denotes an octal integer literal?
questions.explanation: 0o and 0O denote octal literals.

questions.prompt: What does ord() accept in the ordinary use taught here?
questions.explanation: ord returns the Unicode code point of one character.

questions.prompt: What does chr() return for a valid code point?
questions.explanation: chr converts an integer code point to its character.

questions.prompt: What is the standard ASCII code range?
questions.explanation: ASCII has 128 code values; Python strings support Unicode beyond ASCII.

questions.prompt: When does a function body normally execute?

options.text: Whenever its name appears in a comment
Every time any variable is assigned

questions.explanation: A function definition creates a function; a call executes its body.

questions.prompt: What is a parameter?

options.text: A name in a function definition that receives an argument
A line printed by the function
Only a literal in a function call

questions.explanation: Parameters occur in definitions; arguments are supplied by calls.

questions.prompt: What is an argument?

options.text: A value or expression supplied to a function call
Always a variable defined inside the function

questions.explanation: Arguments provide input values for parameter binding.

questions.prompt: Which module comes with the Python standard library?
questions.explanation: math is in the standard library; the other choices are external packages.

questions.prompt: Which command installs an external package from a terminal?
questions.explanation: Package installation and importing in a script are separate operations.

questions.prompt: What does id(obj) guarantee during that object's lifetime?

options.text: A unique value forever across all runs
The number of variable names referring to it
A constant identity value unique among simultaneously existing objects

questions.explanation: Identity values can be reused after an object's lifetime ends.

questions.prompt: What does sys.getrefcount(obj) normally add while inspecting an ordinary non-immortal object?

options.text: A temporary reference for the argument
A guarantee that its count is exactly two

questions.explanation: Exact counts can depend on runtime details and additional references.

questions.prompt: Which claim is safe for portable Python code?

options.text: Equal integer literals always have different identities
id(1000) is a fixed number on every machine
Equal integer literals always have identical identities

questions.explanation: Caching and constant reuse are implementation details.

questions.prompt: What does {:.2f} request in string formatting?

options.text: Fixed-point formatting with two digits after the decimal point
Two significant digits in all cases

questions.explanation: Formatting controls the displayed text; it does not change the original value.

questions.prompt: What does {:,} request for an integer?
questions.explanation: The comma option inserts grouping separators.

questions.prompt: Which statement about help() is correct?

options.text: It executes every function in a module
It guarantees the function has no bugs

questions.explanation: help inspects documentation for an object or module.

questions.prompt: Which keyword starts an ordinary function definition?
questions.explanation: A function definition begins with def and ends its header with a colon.

questions.prompt: What does a function return if execution reaches the end without return?
questions.explanation: An implicit return produces None.

questions.prompt: What does a bare return statement do?

options.text: Exits every function in the program
Returns None and ends the current call

questions.explanation: return exits the current function call.

questions.prompt: What is a docstring?

options.text: A string literal placed first in a function body to document it

questions.explanation: A function docstring describes purpose, parameters and results.

questions.prompt: Which ordinary positional-parameter header is valid?
questions.explanation: A required positional parameter must precede one with a default; a colon is required.

questions.prompt: What does a nested function mean?

options.text: A function that must call itself
A function whose name contains an underscore
A function defined inside another function

questions.explanation: Nesting concerns where the definition occurs.

questions.prompt: What does a call frame represent in the course diagrams?

options.text: One active function call and its local bindings

questions.explanation: Different calls have separate frames, even for the same function.

questions.prompt: What happens to the active call frame when an ordinary call finishes?

options.text: It is removed from the active call stack
It is reused as a list

questions.explanation: Objects referenced elsewhere can remain alive after the call ends.

questions.prompt: Which statement about methods is accurate?

options.text: A method always needs a parameter literally named self
Every callable must be a method
A method is associated with an object or class

questions.explanation: Instance methods conventionally use self; static methods show why the blanket self rule is too broad.

questions.prompt: What happens if a function returns a value but the caller does not save or print it in a script?

options.text: The value is not automatically printed
The value becomes a global variable

questions.explanation: Script execution does not echo arbitrary returned values.

questions.prompt: What does global x inside a function declare?

options.text: Assignments to x use the module-level binding
x is copied into every module
x belongs to the nearest enclosing function

questions.explanation: global refers to the defining module's global namespace.

questions.prompt: What does nonlocal x refer to?

options.text: An existing binding in an enclosing function scope
Any global variable with that name

questions.explanation: nonlocal searches enclosing function scopes, excluding globals.

questions.prompt: What happens if nonlocal names no binding in any enclosing function?

options.text: NameError only at the final print
A global variable is silently created

questions.explanation: A suitable enclosing binding must exist.

questions.prompt: Why can reading x before an assignment to x in the same function fail?

options.text: The assignment makes x local unless declared otherwise

questions.explanation: Reading the unbound local name raises UnboundLocalError.

questions.prompt: What does import math normally bind?

options.text: The name math to a module object
A copy of the entire interpreter
Every math function as an unqualified global name

questions.explanation: Module members are then accessed through math.member.

questions.prompt: After import math as m, how should sqrt be accessed through that import?
questions.explanation: The alias m is the bound module name.

questions.prompt: Which is valid import syntax?
questions.explanation: from module import name binds the selected member.

questions.prompt: What is a risk of from math import *?
questions.explanation: Wildcard imports can introduce name collisions.

questions.prompt: What is a typical Python module?

options.text: A .py file containing definitions and statements

questions.explanation: Modules organize related code and have their own namespaces.

questions.prompt: In math.sin(x), which angular unit is used?

options.text: The unit is inferred from x

questions.explanation: Convert degrees to radians before using trigonometric math functions.

questions.prompt: Which module is associated with pseudorandom selection?
questions.explanation: random contains tools such as choice for selecting sequence elements.

questions.prompt: Which module is associated with Python interpreter information?
questions.explanation: sys exposes interpreter-related facilities; os is more directly about OS interfaces.

questions.prompt: Which is a real application of string matching?
questions.explanation: Spam filtering may search and compare textual patterns.

questions.prompt: What does len('A B') count?

options.text: All three characters, including the space

questions.explanation: Spaces are characters in strings.

questions.prompt: What is the index of the final character in a nonempty string using negative indexing?
questions.explanation: Negative indexing counts backward from the end.

questions.prompt: What does the stop bound of a slice mean?

options.text: It must equal the string length

questions.explanation: s[start:stop] includes start but excludes stop.

questions.prompt: What happens when a string slice extends beyond the string length?
questions.explanation: An out-of-range single index is different from a clipped slice.

questions.prompt: Which slice step is invalid?
questions.explanation: A zero step raises ValueError.

questions.prompt: What does string immutability prohibit?

options.text: Rebinding a variable to a new string
Assigning directly to an individual character position

questions.explanation: The existing string cannot be mutated, but new strings can be assigned.

questions.prompt: What does s.find('z') return if z is absent?
questions.explanation: find uses -1 for a missing substring.

questions.prompt: What does s.index('z') do if z is absent?
questions.explanation: index and find differ in their handling of absence.

questions.prompt: How does strip('ab') interpret its argument?

options.text: As exactly the substring ab to remove once
As a set of characters removable from both ends

questions.explanation: strip repeatedly removes matching edge characters and stops at others.

questions.prompt: What distinguishes split() from split(' ')?

options.text: split() collapses runs of whitespace and drops edge empty fields

questions.explanation: An explicit separator preserves empty fields between adjacent separators.

questions.prompt: What must ordinary elements passed to str.join be?
questions.explanation: join concatenates strings; it does not implicitly convert integers.

questions.prompt: Which operation returns a string with each word title-cased?
questions.explanation: capitalize changes the first character and lowercases the remainder; title works on word boundaries.

questions.prompt: What does the escape sequence backslash-n represent?

options.text: A literal n in every string

questions.explanation: Escapes allow special characters inside string literals.

questions.prompt: Can random.choice('ABCDE') be assumed always to return C?

options.text: No, it selects an element and the exact result is not fixed here
No, it always returns an index
Yes, it always chooses the middle

questions.explanation: A valid question asks about possible results rather than an unspecified random outcome.

questions.prompt: What is a precondition?

options.text: An instruction that always raises an error
An assumption required before an operation
The final line of a program

questions.explanation: A precondition describes the inputs or state under which the contract applies.

questions.prompt: What follows from violating a documented precondition?

options.text: An error must always be printed
The specification no longer guarantees the intended result
The function must always return None

questions.explanation: A violation may cause an error or an unintended result without an error.

questions.prompt: What should a useful test case include?

options.text: Only a screenshot of the editor

questions.explanation: Expected results make pass/fail comparison possible.

questions.prompt: What is debugging?

options.text: Writing a docstring without inspecting behavior
Only running a correct program once

questions.explanation: Testing exposes failures; debugging investigates and corrects causes.

questions.prompt: What is a syntax error?

options.text: A violation of Python's grammatical rules

questions.explanation: A script must parse before ordinary execution begins.

questions.prompt: What is the relationship between IndentationError and SyntaxError?

options.text: IndentationError is a kind of SyntaxError
SyntaxError is a kind of ZeroDivisionError
IndentationError occurs only after all output

questions.explanation: Indentation is part of Python syntax.

questions.prompt: A program runs but computes the wrong formula. What is the clearest diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The slides use overlapping semantic/logical terminology; an incorrect result need not raise an exception.

questions.prompt: Which standard-library module supports debugging?
questions.explanation: pdb is Python's debugger.

questions.prompt: Does passing a finite collection of tests prove correctness for every input?

options.text: Yes, if no print statements are used
Yes, if there are at least ten
Yes, if every test uses integers

questions.explanation: Untested cases may still expose bugs.

questions.prompt: What exception does a false assert normally raise?
questions.explanation: Assertions check assumptions when assertion execution is enabled.

questions.prompt: Why should production input validation not rely only on assert?

options.text: Assertions can be disabled by optimization

questions.explanation: Use explicit checks and suitable exceptions for required validation.

questions.prompt: When does try-else execute in a simple try-except-else statement?

options.text: Only when finally raises an exception
When the try suite completes normally without an exception

questions.explanation: else is for the normal successful path.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of finally in ordinary exception handling?

options.text: Cleanup on both normal completion and exception propagation

questions.explanation: finally normally runs when leaving the try statement, including during return or propagation.

questions.prompt: What happens to an exception not matched by a local except clause?

options.text: It is always converted to None
It propagates to an enclosing handler or terminates execution if uncaught

questions.explanation: Only matching handlers handle that exception.

questions.prompt: How many branches of one if-elif-else chain execute during one pass?
questions.explanation: The first true condition wins; else handles the remaining case.

questions.prompt: How do separate if statements differ from an if-elif chain?

options.text: An elif chain evaluates every body
Separate if statements cannot use comparisons
Several separate if bodies may execute

questions.explanation: Each independent if performs its own test.

questions.prompt: Does else take its own condition?
questions.explanation: else is the catch-all branch and uses a colon without a condition.

questions.prompt: What controls which if an else belongs to?
questions.explanation: Correct indentation determines nesting and branch association.

questions.prompt: What is a danger of testing score >= 50 before score >= 90 in an elif chain?

options.text: The code always has a syntax error
The broader first condition captures high scores too

questions.explanation: Arrange overlapping tests so the intended categories are reachable.

questions.prompt: Which tests are important around a cutoff of 60?

options.text: Values just below, equal to, and just above 60

questions.explanation: Boundary tests expose mistakes involving < versus <=.

questions.prompt: Does a normal if statement introduce a separate function-style local scope?

options.text: Only when the condition is false

questions.explanation: A binding created in an executed if suite belongs to its enclosing scope.

questions.prompt: Can a skipped branch contain a runtime-failing operation without raising it?

options.text: Only if it is a comment
No, every operation executes while parsing
Yes, if that operation is never executed

questions.explanation: Runtime operations in skipped branches do not run; syntax still must be valid.

questions.prompt: What is memory management concerned with?

options.text: Allocation, deallocation and coordination of memory

questions.explanation: Programs need memory for data and instructions.

questions.prompt: Which mechanisms are discussed for CPython memory reclamation?

options.text: Only manual free() calls in user code

questions.explanation: Reference counting and cyclic garbage collection complement one another.

questions.prompt: What does a new alias to an ordinary object generally do?

options.text: Adds a reference to the same object

questions.explanation: Two names can refer to a single object.

questions.prompt: Does del a necessarily destroy the object formerly referenced by a?

options.text: Yes, if the name is one character
No, other references may keep it alive
Yes, in every implementation and situation
No, because objects can never be reclaimed

questions.explanation: Deleting a binding and destroying an object are different events.

questions.prompt: Why is cyclic garbage collection useful?

options.text: Unreachable cycles can retain nonzero reference counts
It proves all memory is leak-free

questions.explanation: Reference counting alone cannot reclaim some unreachable reference cycles.

questions.prompt: In the course's conceptual diagrams, where are object instances represented?

options.text: In a separate interpreter per variable

questions.explanation: Names and frames refer to objects in the conceptual heap model.

questions.prompt: What does the raw allocator interact with at the lowest level?
questions.explanation: Higher-level object-specific allocators operate within the managed memory system.

questions.prompt: Why have object-specific allocators?

options.text: Different object types have different storage requirements and tradeoffs
To make every object occupy the same bytes
To prevent any object from being freed

questions.explanation: Allocation policies can differ by object kind.

questions.prompt: Which call normally finishes first when f calls g and g calls h?

options.text: The function defined first in the file

questions.explanation: The currently deepest ordinary call completes before its caller resumes.

questions.prompt: What belongs to one active call's frame in the teaching model?

options.text: Every object in the operating system

questions.explanation: Frames track the state of individual calls.

questions.prompt: Can an object created in a function remain alive after that function returns?

options.text: Yes, if a reference to it survives
Only if it is an integer literal
Only if its name is global
No, all such objects must immediately disappear

questions.explanation: Returning a list can preserve it after the producing frame is no longer active.

questions.prompt: How is a function definition different from a call frame?

options.text: They are always the same object
The function object can be reused; a frame represents a particular call
A definition is recreated for every arithmetic operation
A frame stores only the filename

questions.explanation: Multiple calls can refer to one function object while using separate frames.

questions.prompt: What does import math place in the importing namespace?

options.text: A binding to a module object
Independent bare bindings for every math member

questions.explanation: The course diagram shows math referring to the module containing its members.

questions.prompt: Which statement about Python lists is correct?
questions.explanation: A list stores an ordered sequence of references and may contain mixed types.

questions.prompt: Which expression constructs an empty list?
questions.explanation: [] is another empty-list expression; {} is a dictionary and () a tuple.

questions.prompt: What does append(x) add?

options.text: Only a shallow copy of x
Every element of x in all cases
One object as one new element

questions.explanation: Appending a list creates a nested element rather than flattening it.

questions.prompt: What does extend(iterable) do?

options.text: Appends the iterable as a single object

questions.explanation: extend consumes the iterable and mutates the receiving list.

questions.prompt: What does pop() do when called without an index on a nonempty list?

options.text: Removes and returns the last element

questions.explanation: The default index is -1.

questions.prompt: What does remove(value) remove?

options.text: The element at numeric position value

questions.explanation: remove uses equality to find a value and raises ValueError if missing.

questions.prompt: How does list.sort() differ from sorted(list)?

options.text: sort mutates and returns None; sorted returns a new list

questions.explanation: Do not assign a.sort() when the intention is a sorted list result.

questions.prompt: What is list.reverse() designed to do?

options.text: Reverse the current order in place
Sort numerically descending in all cases

questions.explanation: Reversing order and sorting descending are different operations.

questions.prompt: When are mutable default parameter values evaluated?
questions.explanation: A default list may therefore be shared across calls.

questions.prompt: How can a function give each defaulted call a fresh list?

options.text: Use [] as the default and assume it is recreated
Use None as a default and create a list inside when needed

questions.explanation: A sentinel avoids unintentionally sharing one mutable default object.

questions.prompt: What does list.count(x) return?

options.text: The total length regardless of x
The index of the first element

questions.explanation: count counts occurrences; index locates the first matching occurrence.

questions.prompt: What does b = a do when a is a list?

options.text: Makes b an alias of the same list

questions.explanation: Assignment alone does not copy a list.

questions.prompt: What does a[:] create for a list?

options.text: A new outer list with references to the same elements

questions.explanation: Nested mutable elements remain shared in a shallow copy.

questions.prompt: What does list(a) do when a is a list?
questions.explanation: list(a), a[:] and a.copy() make shallow copies of an ordinary list.

questions.prompt: Which statement about extend and + is correct?

options.text: They always have identical aliasing behavior
extend mutates the list; + creates a new concatenated list

questions.explanation: Their resulting contents may agree while mutation and return values differ.

questions.prompt: How is an element in a nested list normally accessed?

options.text: Only with a single index counting every nested value

questions.explanation: For example grid[row][column] selects an element in a row.

questions.prompt: What is the default starting counter of enumerate()?
questions.explanation: Use start=1 or another value to change labels.

questions.prompt: What does changing enumerate(items, start=5) change?

options.text: The first item selected from items

questions.explanation: start is a counter offset, not a slicing bound.

questions.prompt: What does a list comprehension produce?

options.text: Only an iterator in all cases
A mutated source list in all cases

questions.explanation: It evaluates an expression for selected items of an iterable.

questions.prompt: Where does a filtering if go in a basic list comprehension?
questions.explanation: The pattern is [expression for item in iterable if condition].

questions.prompt: What is a lambda expression?

options.text: An anonymous function defined by an expression
A command to copy every object
A loop that always runs forever

questions.explanation: lambda parameters: expression evaluates to a function.

questions.prompt: Which object properties are listed in the lecture?

options.text: Type, internal representation and supported operations
Only the number of characters printed

questions.explanation: An object is an instance of a type; a variable name is a reference to an object.
